Strategic Focus – Healthy, Safe and Inclusive Communities
PHP-CFH-23-001, Supporting Healthy Early Child Development Including a New Indigenous Led Program
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner of Public Health and Paramedic Services, provided a brief overview the presentation, which is attached to the agenda, and introduced Janet McCreary, Manager, Healthy Babies Healthy Children Program and Charisse Sayer, Integrated Care Manager, SOAHAC. The purpose of the report is to develop culturally appropriate Indigenous-led Healthy Child Development program through the partnership with the Region and SOAHAC.

The Committee acknowledged the significant impact of SOAHAC for the Indigenous community in the Region of Waterloo, specifically, it was noted that SOAHAC guided the vaccine rollout to ensure that it was accessible to the Indigenous community.

The report was received for information.

items.title: PHP-HLV-23-001, Waterloo Region Integrated Drug Strategy and Public Health’s Work within the Strategy
notes:
H. Wang provided a brief overview of the presentation, which is attached to the agenda. She described the role of the Waterloo Region Integrated Drug Strategy (WRIDS) in the community and introduced their representatives Erica Poulin, Eugene Fenton, Michelle Kennedy,  Lindsay Sprague, Violet Umanetz and Leigh Wardlaw. They explained the four pillar approach which is prevention, harm reduction, recovery and rehabilitation and enforcement and justice. L. Wardlaw provided background on programs Working to Improve Neighbourhood Safety (WINS) and V. Umanetz provided background on the program Consumption and Treatment (CTS) Site and they noted the number of drug poisonings that were reversed between January-December 2022. 

The Committee acknowledged the good works of WRIDS and requested a copy of the 2022 Drug Policy Position Paper that was referenced in the presentation.

In response to the Committee, H. Wang explained that the approval for Consumption and Treatment sites are provincially mandated and currently there is one site in the Region of Waterloo. V. Umanetz added that Consumption and Treatment sites allow individuals to build relationships with Staff which has resulted in many positive outcomes such as those individuals moving on to using the program Working to Improve Neighbourhood Safety.

In response to the Committee, E. Fenton noted that the new communication coordinator will be upgrading many aspects of WRIDS community engagement including their website. Jonathan Mall Manager, Healthy Living & Smoke Free Ontario explained the difference between Overdose Monitoring Alert and Response System (OMARS) and the dashboard as the dashboard is a collection of data whereas OMARS is to alert the community of certain activities such as current overdose situations. He also explained that expansions to Consumption and Treatment sites are needed to decrease overdoses in the Community such as increased open hours and establish inhalation services.

In response to the Committee, L. Sprague explained that a major barrier to the WRIDS programs is funding and supporting Staff. They also noted that municipal advocacy is essential to maintain and expand services in the Region of Waterloo. J. Mall further explained the importance of collaboration between WRIDS and the Region of Waterloo.  E. Fenton noted that WRIDS began a new program in January 2023 and will be establishing new objectives including minimizing the stigma surrounding drug use. H. Wang also noted that public health is a partner of WRIDS.

The Committee directed Staff to advocate to the Ministry regarding the inclusion of inhalation supplies at Consumption and Treatment (CTS) Sites.. Also, the Committee directed Staff to provide an update on current drug use statistics in the Region without the use of proxy measures. H. Wang explained that the dashboard is the most recent data, but proxy measures have to be used as drug use has to be an estimate due to the lack personal disclosure of drug use.

The report was received for information.

items.title: CSD-HOU-23-008, Regulatory Changes to Housing Services Act, 2011
notes: Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, introduced Ryan Pettipiere, Director of Housing Services, and Jennifer Murdoch, Manager, Housing Programs to provide a presentation, which is attached to the agenda. R. Pettipiere provided background of the regulatory changes to the Housing Services Act, 2011. Specifically, he discussed the legislation was silent on how to manage the  manage the funding model in the absence of a mortgage. J. Murdoch described the community housing succession strategy which is intended to set a path forward for the delivery of community housing in the Region and the community in a post-end of mortgage (EOM) operating environment. The succession strategy has several goals such as establishing a responsive affordable housing system. R. Pettipiere concluded with next steps that include negotiating agreements and funding plans to support financial sustainability of the community housing portfolio.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Responsive and Engaging Public Service
PHP-PSV-23-001, Earlier Implementation of the Medical Priority Dispatching System (MPDS)
notes:
John Riches, Director/Chief of Paramedic Services, provided an overview of the presentation, which is attached to the agenda. He described the current system operates directly through the Cambridge Central Central Ambulance system and is a rigid system that does not support reassignment of Code 4 response regardless of the situation. However, the Province committed in 2019 to implement a new dispatch system known as Medical Priority Dispatch System, which allows for increased medical oversight and accuracy. Paramedic Services support the transition to the new Medical Priority Dispatch System and J. Riches expressed that potential improvements include code red incidents efficiencies and Staff work-life balance.

The Committee discussed the advantages of transitioning from the current deployment system to the Medical Priority Dispatch system to modernize the system which is aimed to better utilize the Region's paramedic resources through effective medical prioritization.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-23-008, Regulatory Changes to Housing Services Act, 2011
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to take the following actions in response to Ont. Reg. 241/22 and Ont. Reg. 242/22, new regulations under the Housing Services Act , 2011 (HSA) , as described in CSD-HOU-23-008 dated March 7, 2023: Draft and negotiate a funding model that achieves the legislative directives and supports long-term financial sustainability of the community housing portfolio for housing providers to meet their operating and capital needs upon End of Mortgage (EOM); Subject to annual budget approval, direct staff to develop an annual housing reinvestment plan using the funds resulting from community housing provider mortgage maturity for the purpose of: Maintaining or increasing the number of rent-geared-to-income (RGI) units to meet the Region's obligations under the HSA; and Providing capital funding for asset renewal needs of community housing providers; for the renewal and expansion of Waterloo Region Housing properties, including investments within the Waterloo Region Housing Master Plan; and grants to incent the construction of new affordable housing units; Authorize the Commissioner, Community Services to enter into service or exit agreements as housing providers reach EOM in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; Amend the current surplus-sharing practice within the mandated funding model to allow community housing providers to retain annual operating surpluses subject to the following conditions: The amount of the surplus transferred to a provider’s capital reserve is limited such that the balance in the capital reserve will not to exceed the value of capital work identified for the next five years, and; Capping the accumulated surplus at $500/unit; Endorse a new Asset Limit Policy required by Ont. Reg. 242/22 to establish asset limits of $75,000 for single households and $100,000 for households with more than one person for households applying for and receiving rent-geared-to-income (RGI) subsidy.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to take the following actions in response to Ont. Reg. 241/22 and Ont. Reg. 242/22, new regulations under the Housing Services Act, 2011 (HSA), as described in CSD-HOU-23-008 dated March 7, 2023:

  1. Draft and negotiate a funding model that achieves the legislative directives and supports long-term financial sustainability of the community housing portfolio for housing providers to meet their operating and capital needs upon End of Mortgage (EOM);
  2. Subject to annual budget approval, direct staff to develop an annual housing reinvestment plan using the funds resulting from community housing provider mortgage maturity for the purpose of:
    1. Maintaining or increasing the number of rent-geared-to-income (RGI) units to meet the Region's obligations under the HSA; and
    2. Providing capital funding for asset renewal needs of community housing providers; for the renewal and expansion of Waterloo Region Housing properties, including investments within the Waterloo Region Housing Master Plan; and grants to incent the construction of new affordable housing units;
  3. Authorize the Commissioner, Community Services to enter into service or exit agreements as housing providers reach EOM in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor;
  4. Amend the current surplus-sharing practice within the mandated funding model to allow community housing providers to retain annual operating surpluses subject to the following conditions:
    1. The amount of the surplus transferred to a provider’s capital reserve is limited such that the balance in the capital reserve will not to exceed the value of capital work identified for the next five years, and;
    2. Capping the accumulated surplus at $500/unit; 
  5. Endorse a new Asset Limit Policy required by Ont. Reg. 242/22 to establish asset limits of $75,000 for single households and $100,000 for households with more than one person for households applying for and receiving rent-geared-to-income (RGI) subsidy.

motions.item_title: PHP-PSV-23-001, Earlier Implementation of the Medical Priority Dispatching System (MPDS)
motions.text: Due to the high volume of calls causing lack of availability of paramedic resources and life saving measures, the Regional Municipality of Waterloo fully supports the Medical Priority Dispatch System, requests that the Ministry of Health adopt a Medical Priority Dispatch System at the Cambridge Central Ambulance Communications Centre as soon as possible; And that the Region of Waterloo Paramedic Services Chief and Deputy Chiefs be directed to continue to engage with the Ministry of Health and the Guelph-Wellington and Dufferin County Paramedic Services to support this request; And that the Regional Chair, Council, Chief Administrative Officer, Commissioner and Medical Officer of Health be directed to advocate to Provincial counterparts (Minister of Health, ADM, local MPPs etc.) for the early adoption of a Medical Priority Dispatch System at the Cambridge Central Ambulance Communications Centre.
motions.text_html:
Due to the high volume of calls causing lack of availability of paramedic resources and life saving measures, the Regional Municipality of Waterloo fully supports the Medical Priority Dispatch System, requests that the Ministry of Health adopt a Medical Priority Dispatch System at the Cambridge Central Ambulance Communications Centre as soon as possible;

And that the Region of Waterloo Paramedic Services Chief and Deputy Chiefs be directed to continue to engage with the Ministry of Health and the Guelph-Wellington and Dufferin County Paramedic Services to support this request;

And that the Regional Chair, Council, Chief Administrative Officer, Commissioner and Medical Officer of Health be directed to advocate to Provincial counterparts (Minister of Health, ADM, local MPPs etc.) for the early adoption of a Medical Priority Dispatch System at the Cambridge Central Ambulance Communications Centre.
